verses.text: This is the blessing Moses, the man of God, gave the Israelites before he died.

He said: "The LORD came from Mount Sinai and rose like the sun over them from Seir. He shone out from Mount Paran. He came with tens of thousands of holy ones, with flaming fire at his right hand for them.
Truly he loves his people. All his holy ones are in your hand. They bow down at your feet, and each one receives your words.
Moses gave us the law, a treasure for the people of Jacob.
The LORD became king over Jeshurun when the leaders of the people gathered, all the tribes of Israel together.
Let Reuben live and not die, and let his people not be few."
This is what he said about Judah: "LORD, hear the cry of Judah, and bring him back to his people. With his own hands he fights for himself. Help him against his enemies!"
About Levi he said: "LORD, your Thummim and Urim belong to your faithful servant. You tested him at Massah and argued with him at the waters of Meribah.
He said of his father and mother, 'I do not care about them.' He did not take the side of his brothers or his own children. For the Levites obeyed your word and kept your covenant.
They will teach your laws to Jacob and your teaching to Israel. They will offer incense before you and whole burnt offerings on your altar.
LORD, bless all his skills, and be pleased with the work of his hands. Crush the backs of those who rise against him. Strike down those who hate him, so that they never rise again."
About Benjamin he said: "Let the one the LORD loves live safely beside him. The LORD protects him all day long, and the one the LORD loves rests between his shoulders."
About Joseph he said: "May the LORD bless his land with the precious gifts of heaven above, with dew, and with the deep waters that lie below.
May it have the best crops the sun brings and the finest fruit each month can give,
with the best gifts of the ancient mountains and the riches of the everlasting hills,

with the best gifts of the earth and everything in it, and the kindness of the one who appeared in the burning bush. Let all these blessings rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the one who was a prince among his brothers.

He has the majesty of a firstborn bull. His horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he will push back the nations, even those at the ends of the earth. Such are the tens of thousands of Ephraim, and such are the thousands of Manasseh."
About Zebulun he said: "Be glad, Zebulun, when you go out, and you, Issachar, in your tents.
They will call the peoples to the mountain and offer right sacrifices there. They will feast on the riches of the seas and the treasures hidden in the sand."
About Gad he said: "Blessed is the one who makes Gad's land larger! Gad lives there like a lion, tearing at arm and head.
He chose the best land for himself. The share of a leader was kept for him. When the leaders of the people gathered, he carried out the LORD's justice and his laws for Israel."
About Dan he said: "Dan is a lion's cub, leaping out from Bashan."
About Naphtali he said: "Naphtali is full of the LORD's favour and filled with his blessing. He will take over the land to the west and the south."
About Asher he said: "Asher is the most blessed of the sons. May he be loved by his brothers, and may his land be rich with olive oil.
May the bars of your gates be iron and bronze, and may your strength last as long as you live.
There is no one like the God of Jeshurun, who rides across the heavens to help you, across the skies in his majesty.
The eternal God is your safe home, and his everlasting arms are under you. He drove out your enemy ahead of you, saying, 'Destroy them!'
So Israel will live in safety. Jacob's descendants will live alone in a land of grain and new wine, where the heavens drop dew.

How happy you are, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD? He is your shield and helper, and your glorious sword. Your enemies will bow before you, and you will walk on their high places."
